q: 1. The diagrammatic representation of the activity of the entire project is called
explain: A network diagram, flow diagram, and control charts are all methods used to represent the various activities and progress of an entire project visually.

q: 2. The pictorial representation of activities and events of a project is known as
explain: In project management, a network (net work) is the specific pictorial representation that shows the relationship between activities and events.

q: 3. In histogram, more prominent will be the differences in heights between the bars if
explain: When the range of data is small, the scale of the histogram allows for more distinct and prominent visual differences between the heights of individual bars.

q: 4. Gantt chart indicates
options: balance of work to be done
comparison of actual progress with the scheduled progress
explain: The primary purpose of a Gantt (Bar) chart is to provide a visual comparison between the actual progress of tasks and the original schedule.

q: 5. In a bar chart the length of horizontal lines for activity A and B are 2 cm and 4 cm respectively. Which one is correct about the activity A & B?
options: activity 'B' need more duration for completion
activity 'A' need more duration for completion
completion time for activities 'A' and 'B' are same
explain: In a bar chart, the length of the horizontal bar represents the duration; therefore, a longer bar (4 cm) indicates a longer time required for completion than a shorter bar (2 cm).

q: 6. Henry Gnatt developed the bar chart technique in
explain: Henry Gantt developed his namesake bar chart technique around 1900 AD to help supervisors see whether they were on schedule.

q: 7. Bar charts are considered suitable for
explain: Bar charts are best suited for minor or simple projects because they lack the ability to show complex interdependencies between hundreds of tasks.

q: 8. Which types of network was first developed for planning of any project?
explain: The bar chart was the earliest formal tool used for project planning, predating more complex network methods like CPM and PERT.

q: 9. On a bar chart the various activities of a project are shown by
explain: Activities in a bar chart are represented by horizontal lines (bars) where the X-axis typically represents time.

q: 10. Job going ahead of schedule are conveniently shown in
explain: Gantt charts allow managers to shade or mark bars to indicate that progress is ahead of the current date line.

q: 11. The upper portion of horizontal bars in a bar chart indicates
options: total duration for completion of an activity
progress of work in the specified time
due duration for the completion of an activity
explain: In specialized bar charts, the upper portion of the bar is often used to shade or hatch the actual progress made relative to the total scheduled duration.

q: 12. Gantt/Bar chart is drawn for
explain: A Gantt chart plots activities on the vertical axis against a time scale on the horizontal axis.

q: 13. The limitations of bar chart are
explain: Bar charts fail to show how activities depend on each other, do not easily account for project uncertainties, and have limited ability to show detailed progress for complex tasks.

q: 14. The weakness in bar charts is
options: uncertainty in duration for various activities
the sequence of activities is not very clear
explain: Because they are simple linear representations, bar charts cannot clearly show the complex sequence or the impact of uncertain durations on the whole project.

q: 15. Gantt chart is drawn for
explain: This is a reiteration that the fundamental layout of a Gantt chart is activities plotted against a timeline.

q: 16. A drawn back of bar chart is
options: it is difficult to judge whether an activity is completed or not
all the activities represented are independent of each other
sequence of activities is not clearly defined
it is not possible to judge whether the activity is ahead or behind the schedule
explain: While progress can be marked, the primary structural drawback is that the specific logical sequence and dependencies between activities are not explicitly defined.

q: 17. Time and progress chart of a construction is known as
explain: Bar charts, Gantt charts, and CPM networks are all variations of time and progress management tools used in construction.

q: 18. A milestone chart
options: shows the interdependence of various jobs
shows the events in chronological, but not in a logical sequence
explain: Milestone charts focus on specific points in time (events) in order, but they do not show the logical 'why' or 'how' between them like a network.

q: 19. Milestone charts are developed in
explain: Milestone charts were developed as an improvement over the basic bar chart around 1940 AD.

q: 20. Mile stones are
explain: A milestone represents a significant event, such as the start or completion (beginning or end) of a group of activities.

q: 21. The interrelationship between the functional elements of a programme is achieved through
explain: Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) decomposes a project into smaller components to define the interrelationships of functional elements.

q: 22. CPM means
explain: CPM is a standard acronym for Critical Path Method, used for project scheduling.

q: 23. CPM adopts
explain: Unlike PERT (which is probabilistic), CPM is deterministic because it assumes activity durations are known with certainty.

q: 24. CPM network is
explain: CPM focuses on the activities themselves (tasks), whereas PERT is event-oriented.

q: 25. A CPM family includes
explain: CPM methodology encompasses analysis, plotting, and scheduling techniques collectively.

q: 26. In CPM analysis
explain: CPM relies on activity-on-arrow representation, assumes fixed durations (no uncertainty), and focuses on activity management.

q: 27. Choose the incorrect statement
options: arrow representing activity in CPM network is drawn without any scale
head of an activity represents the finish of an activity
tail of an activity represents the start of an activity
explain: All the statements provided (a, b, and c) are actually correct definitions within CPM networking; therefore, none are incorrect.

q: 28. The occurrence of the starting of an activity is called its
explain: In activity-on-arrow diagrams, the event at the start (tail) of the arrow is the tail event.

q: 29. The occurrence of the completion of an activity is called its
explain: The event at the end (pointy head) of the arrow signifies the completion of that activity.

q: 30. The difference between total float and free float is called interferring float which is nothing but the
explain: Interfering float equals the head event slack; it is the part of total float that causes delay in succeeding activities if used.

q: 31. The scheduled completion time of an operation in CPM chart is mentioned on
options: left top corner outside the circle
left top corner inside the circle
explain: Standard notation for event circles in CPM often places the earliest expected time at the top left outside the circle.

q: 32. Which operation must complete first?
options: right of the line joining two circles
left of the line joining two circles
explain: In network logic, progress moves from left to right; therefore, activities on the left must be completed before those on the right.

q: 33. Number of pre-operation associated with an operation may be
explain: An activity can have any number of preceding (pre-operation) tasks that must be finished before it starts.

q: 34. In a network, the activity which neither takes time nor resources is called
explain: A dummy activity (sometimes called redundant/null in specific contexts) is a logical link that uses zero time and zero resources.

q: 35. The maximum number of tail event occurring in a CPM is
explain: A standard project network should have only one single start event (tail event) from which the project begins.

q: 36. The maximum number of head event occurring in a CPM is
explain: Similarly, a project network should converge to exactly one single end event (head event).

q: 37. The maximum number of redundant activity in a CPM chart may be
explain: Depending on the complexity and poor logic of a network, any number of activities might be rendered redundant or unnecessary.

q: 38. The activity which consumes maximum time is called
explain: The 'critical path' is the longest path, but a single activity consuming 'maximum time' is not a standard definition for a specific activity type in this context.

q: 39. The number of post-activity associated with head event may be
explain: The final head event (end of project) has no subsequent activities (post-activities) following it.

q: 40. The post-operations in CPM are marked
explain: In chronological flow, subsequent operations (post-operations) are placed to the right of the current task.

q: 41. In CPM method, the earliest finish is indicated by time on
options: top right, outside the circle, in triangle
top right, outside the circle, in rectangle
explain: The Earliest Finish Time (EFT) or Earliest Start Time (EST) is often noted in a square/rectangle near the event node.

q: 42. Latest finish time in CPM technique is indicated by
explain: Standard CPM notation uses rectangles (or squares) to denote time values like Latest Finish Time.

q: 43. When the times of earliest finish and the latest finish are equal in an operation, the operation is called
explain: If the earliest and latest times are equal, there is zero float, making that activity critical.

q: 44. An example for a parallel activity is
options: completing ground floor and starting first floor
wall and carpentry work of doors and windows
completion of flooring and initiating white washing
digging of a well and of septic tank
explain: Parallel activities can happen simultaneously; wall construction and carpentry can often proceed at the same time in different sections.

q: 45. A dummy activity
options: had no tail event but had only a head event
had only a head event but no tail event
does not require any resources or any time
had no sequence and can be fitted anywhere
explain: A dummy activity is a purely logical connection used to show dependency without adding time or cost to the project.

q: 46. Critical path is
options: shortest path for the earliest completion of the project
longest path of the network from the first event to the last event
ideal path by preceeding along which the project can be completed as per the schedule
the path which takes into account the completion of all the parallel activities
explain: The critical path is the specific sequence of activities that must be completed exactly as scheduled to finish the project on time.

q: 47. The minimum number of critical path in a net work should be
explain: Every project network must have at least one critical path connecting the start to the end.

q: 48. Critical path network helps the engineer to
options: concentrate his attention on critical activitirs
divert the different resourced from non-critical activities to critical activities
be cautious for avoiding any delay in the critical activities
explain: CPM analysis allows engineers to focus on the most important tasks and manage resources across the project efficiently.

q: 49. In CPM, 'Forward Pass' and 'Backward Pass' are used to calculate respectively.
options: earliest expected time and latest allowable time
latest allowable time and earliest expected time
explain: Forward pass calculates Earliest times; Backward pass calculates Latest times.

q: 50. Float is
options: the earliest time by which an activity may commence
latest time by which an activity can be delayed without hampering the completion of the project
time available-time required for an activity
explain: Float represents the extra time available for an activity beyond what is actually required for its execution.

q: 51. Positive float can occur when it is
explain: A sub-critical activity has a positive float, meaning it has extra time available and does not currently sit on the critical path.

q: 52. Negative float can occur when it is
explain: Negative float occurs in super-critical activities where the time required exceeds the time available, indicating the project is behind schedule.

q: 53. The estimated time required to complete an activity is termed as
explain: Duration is the standard term in project management for the estimated time needed to perform a specific task or activity.

q: 54. Free float is mainly used to
options: identify the activities which can be delayed without affecting the total float of preceeding activity
identify the activities, which can be delayed without affecting the total float of succeeding activity
identify the activities which can be delayed without affecting the total float of either the preceeding or succeeding activities
explain: Free float is the amount of time an activity can be delayed without affecting the earliest start time of any immediately following (succeeding) activities.

q: 55. Whenever activity has zero total float, then
options: free float of the activity must be zero but independent float need not be zero
independent float must be zero but free float need not be zero
free float and independent float both must be zero
free float and independent float both need not be zero
explain: Since total float is the 'parent' float, if it is zero, all other sub-types of float (free and independent) must also be zero.

q: 56. Total float for any activity is defined as the difference between
options: its latest finish time and earliest start time for its successor activity
its latest start time and earliest start time
its latest start time and earliest finish time
its earliest finish time and earliest start time for its successor activity
explain: Total float is calculated as (Latest Start - Earliest Start) or (Latest Finish - Earliest Finish).

q: 57. Free float for any activity is defined as the difference between
options: its latest start time and earliest start time for its successor activity
its latest start time and earliest start time
its latest finish time and earliest start time for its successor activity
its earliest finish time and earliest start time for its successor activity
explain: Free float is the Earliest Start of the successor minus the Earliest Finish of the current activity.

q: 58. The time by which a particular activity may be delayed without affecting the preceeding and succeeding activities is known as
explain: Independent float is unique because it doesn't affect the float of activities coming before or after it.

q: 59. Which of the following in a CPM network activity?
explain: In CPM, an 'activity' is an active process that consumes time and resources; 'excavation' is a clear action, while the others are often viewed as states/events.

q: 60. According to Fulkerson's, the correct event numbers corresponding to event A, B, C, D, E of the network shown in figure
explain: Fulkerson's Rule (I-J numbering) requires that the number at the head of an arrow is always greater than the number at the tail.

q: 61. A fictious activity with zero duration and no cost used to maintain the sequential order of the activities in network is known as a
explain: A dummy activity is a logical link represented by a dashed arrow that consumes no time or resources.

q: 62. Earliest finish time of an activity is always
options: equal to or more than earliest event
equal to or less than earliest event time of the following node
more than earliest time of the following node
explain: The finish time of an activity must occur by the time the following node (event) is reached; it cannot exceed that event's earliest time.

q: 63. Latest start of activity is always
options: less than or equal to latest event time of preceeding node
more than or equal to latest events time of preceeding node
equal to latest event time of preceeding node
explain: The latest an activity can start must be at or after the latest time its preceding event (node) can occur.

q: 64. Latest start time is the
options: latest time by which an activity can be started without delaying the project
latest time by which an activity can be completed without delaying the project
latest time the event can occur
explain: Latest Start Time (LST) is the maximum delay possible for the start of a task that won't push back the project completion date.

q: 65. The difference between the total float and the free float is termed as
explain: Interfering float is the difference between Total Float and Free Float (TF - FF).

q: 66. The independent float affects only
explain: By definition, independent float is the time by which an activity can be delayed without affecting any other activity in the network.

q: 67. The free – float affects only
explain: Free float refers to the flexibility available for an activity itself without impacting the start of successors, effectively only relating to the activity and its predecessors.

q: 68. What are essential to draw CPM ?
explain: CPM is primarily a time-management tool; while resources are important, time estimates for each activity are the fundamental requirement for the network.

q: 69. Critical-path connecting the start and end events time wise is
explain: The critical path is the longest path through a network diagram; any delay on this path delays the entire project.

q: 70. Critical activities having total float are
explain: An activity is critical if its total float is zero, meaning there is no flexibility in its timing.

q: 71. The activity which consumes maximum time is called a
explain: A single activity consuming a lot of time isn't 'called' a specific name in network theory; it is the 'path' that becomes critical.

q: 72. The figure [merging arrows] indicates
explain: When multiple activity arrows point into a single event node, it is known as a merge event.

q: 73. The figure [bursting arrows] indicates
explain: When multiple activity arrows originate from a single event node, it is known as a burst event.

q: 74. Completion of an activity on CPM network diagram, is generally known as
explain: The point in time marking the start or completion of an activity is called an event (represented by a node/circle).

q: 75. Free float is the
explain: Free float is a subset of total float; specifically, it is the portion of total float that can be used without delaying the next activity.
